scope.description: A single Raft node using the in-module NetworkTransport (or any transport that honours SetHeartbeatHandler) with a heartbeat handler registered by NewRaft, while it is handling RPCs. Applies to the current-term context only, not to the log content, the commit index or the configuration.
assumptions: the node is not shut down while the RPCs are processed
the StableStore accepts SetUint64 for the CurrentTerm key, since setCurrentTerm panics otherwise
an RPC with a term greater than the adopted term is a legal event, because appendEntries and requestVote adopt it
excluded: log replication correctness and the commit-index rule (a separate obligation)
the leader-identity fact, which is tracked separately as f-known-leader
behaviour of transports outside this module that do not implement a heartbeat fast path

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: StreamLayer is replaced by an in-process net.Pipe fabric (assurancePipeNet/assurancePipeLayer). NetworkTransport, its heartbeat classification in handleCommand, the SetHeartbeatHandler registration performed by NewRaft, Raft.processHeartbeat and Raft.appendEntries are the target's own code and are not re-implemented.

StableStore is an InmemStore wrapper whose SetUint64 holds exactly one CurrentTerm write. This is a latency injection on an injected dependency; it changes no term comparison, no branch condition and no write performed by the target.
The harness adds one external test file to the captured package and modifies no target file.

plan_uncertainties: The equality encoding coincides with the obligation's 'not lower than' only inside this prefix, where exactly two term writes are admitted (5 then 6) and nothing else can establish a term.

The dispatch of the heartbeat callback off the main goroutine is the documented SetHeartbeatHandler contract and is exercised here with the real NetworkTransport over a substituted StreamLayer; the production TCP deployment's scheduling is a source-level premise of this check rather than an execution result.

The check observes the term context only. It does not observe the downstream consequence, e.g. whether a later vote could be granted in a term the node has already voted in, and it does not test any node other than the one receiving both RPCs.
grounding_unresolved: whether the two goroutines can interleave between the read of currentTerm and the store inside one appendEntries call
whether a concurrent equal-term or greater-term main-loop RPC is required for the hazard, or a single heartbeat suffices
the wire medium is substituted (net.Pipe instead of TCP), so TCP framing and kernel scheduling are not exercised
that NetworkTransport invokes the callback off the main goroutine is established from source and re-used here, not re-derived by the execution
the comparison is equality with the admitted term, which coincides with 'not lower than the admitted term' only because this prefix admits exactly two term writes
